question.prompt:
In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AB=AC.\) If there is a point \(P\) strictly between \(A\) and \(B\) such that \(AP=PC=CB,\) then \(\angle A=\)

[Figure 1](figures/1994_AMC_12_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The equal lengths let us pass angle information through three isosceles triangles. Let \(\theta=\angle BAC\). Since \(P\) lies strictly between \(A\) and \(B\), we also have \(\angle PAC=\theta\).

In triangle \(APC\), the equality \(AP=PC\) gives \(\angle ACP=\angle PAC=\theta\). Its remaining angle is therefore
\[
\angle APC=180^\circ-2\theta.
\]
The rays \(PA\) and \(PB\) point in opposite directions, so \(\angle APC\) and \(\angle BPC\) are supplementary. Hence \(\angle BPC=2\theta\).

Now \(PC=CB\), so triangle \(PCB\) has equal base angles at \(P\) and \(B\). Thus \(\angle PBC=2\theta\), which is also \(\angle ABC\). Finally, \(AB=AC\) gives \(\angle ACB=\angle ABC=2\theta\). The angle sum in triangle \(ABC\) yields
\[
\theta+2\theta+2\theta=180^\circ,
\qquad \theta=36^\circ.
\]
Therefore \(\angle A=\boxed{36^\circ}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Follow the equal base angles
